Show how the projection is calculated

Salary subject to CPF = min(gross salary, $8,000). Employee CPF = 20%; employer CPF = 17%. Each monthly contribution is split using the 2026 age-band allocation table, with age increasing during the projection. OA earns an assumed 2.5% yearly and SA 4%, converted to equivalent monthly growth. Monthly housing withdrawals reduce OA; no borrowing is assumed when OA reaches zero.

Age-55 FRS scenario = $220,400 × (1 + chosen retirement-sum increase)^(55 − age). ERS comparison = twice that scenario FRS. FRS is cohort-specific; actual ERS follows the limit in force when topping up at 55+. This is an accumulation illustration to 55, not a CPF LIFE payout quote.

Excludes bonuses, salary increases, future rule/rate changes, extra interest, MA overflow, account rounding and other withdrawals. MA is excluded from the retirement target. OA + SA coverage assumes OA remains available at 55. Reaching the ERS comparison requires eligible voluntary transfers or top-ups to RA after 55; it does not happen automatically. RA inputs are not projected: use CPF’s own planner at 55+.

How do Endowus / Syfe payouts compare with CPF LIFE?

CPF LIFE: lifelong payout with CPF rules and plan choices. Endowus / Syfe investment payouts: distributions can vary, portfolio values can fall, and a distribution is not the same as a guaranteed return. Compare fees, payout source, capital impact and what happens in a market downturn.

Put the pieces together

Your funding order, from payday to retirement

  1. 1. Keep your base safe.

    Clear costly debt and keep emergency and near-term housing cash accessible. Decide what you can commit for decades.

  2. 2. Check compulsory CPF before adding more.

    The forecast above shows what salary contributions may already achieve. FRS is a useful income-floor checkpoint; ERS is an optional higher-income commitment at 55+, not a requirement for everyone. If you already project to meet your target, extra top-ups need a clear purpose.

  3. 3. Close a chosen CPF gap early, when affordable.

    Compare the early-top-up illustration above. More years of interest helps, but cash top-ups and OA-to-SA/RA transfers are generally irreversible. Check the actual top-up limit in CPF; a top-up ceiling and a tax-relief ceiling are different things.

  4. 4. Decide whether SRS earns its place.

    For citizens/PRs, the cap is $15,300 per year—equivalent to saving $1,275 a month. It is not $15,300 a month. SRS is optional: its value depends on your marginal tax rate, other reliefs, liquidity and withdrawal tax. Total personal income tax relief is capped at $80,000 per year.

    Where to invest SRS money

    Contributing alone leaves cash uninvested. For a long horizon, consider a diversified, low-cost equity fund eligible for SRS, such as an SRS-supported fund portfolio through Endowus; compare fund and platform fees. SRS cannot simply buy any overseas ETF, so do not assume VWRA is available. For near-term spending, assess eligible deposits, SSBs or suitable bonds instead.

    How SRS withdrawals work

    Normal qualifying retirement withdrawals are 50% taxable and can generally be spread across 10 years. Early withdrawals are generally fully taxable plus a 5% penalty, subject to exceptions. Your qualifying retirement age depends on the age prevailing at your first SRS contribution.

    Example SRS investment routes ↗ · IRAS SRS contribution rules ↗
  5. 5. Invest outside CPF / SRS for flexibility.

    Use the monthly saving estimate above for the gap left after your updated CPF LIFE estimate. If you use SRS investments for part of that gap, count those investments once, and allow for withdrawal tax and access dates. Keep an accessible bridge if retiring before CPF LIFE payouts begin.

  6. 6. Gradually prepare cash and bond maturities.

    As spending dates approach, build your chosen cash buffer and fixed-income ladder. Keep long-horizon growth money invested at a risk level you can tolerate, then review the plan once a year.

Make investments easier to spend later

A drawdown plan for the years after work.

If you hold a broad share fund such as VWRA, build a written transition plan over time. A retirement date does not require selling everything at once.

01

Calculate the gap first

Use the monthly plan above. Size investments against spending left after CPF LIFE and any other steady income.

02

Set an accessible spending reserve

Choose how many months of your investment-funded gap to hold in cash or similarly accessible savings, based on comfort and upcoming costs.

03

Build a fixed-income ladder gradually

Match maturities to planned spending. Singapore Savings Bonds can be redeemed monthly without a penalty; allow for processing time, so they are not instant cash.

04

Keep long-horizon money invested

Keep an equity allocation you can tolerate through market falls. Rebalance on a set schedule and use a written rule for replenishing cash after stronger markets.

SINGAPORE SAVINGS BONDS$200,000maximum holding per individual across cash and SRS

Buy in $500 multiples. You can request redemption monthly, with no penalty; proceeds are paid after processing in the following month. Keep near-term bills in a more immediately accessible account.

MAS: SSB limits and redemption ↗

There is no universal “sell VWRA at age X” rule. Decide in advance what the money is for, which spending years are covered by cash and bonds, and when you will rebalance. Investment values and bond rates can change.
